articles.title: Uber is letting parents check in on their teens through drivers’ selfie cameras
articles.summary: Uber is launching a new way for parents to keep tabs on their teen kids during rides by using the driver’s selfie camera.
articles.body: Uber is updating its teen account feature to allow parents to use the selfie cameras on Uber drivers’ phones to check in on their teenage children during ridehail trips. Since first launching teen accounts in 2023, Uber has touted the myriad ways parents can keep tabs on their children, from PIN verification to live GPS tracking. Now, parents can also view live video of the ride while it’s in progress by viewing the feed from the driver’s selfie camera. Uber said that after testing the new feature in several markets, it’s ready to roll out nationwide over the next few weeks. Drivers who have opted in to accept underage passengers will now also be asked to give parents brief access to the selfie cameras on their phones. If they approve, the parent or guardian who’s linked in the teen’s account will receive a push notification when live video is available. The teen and the driver are both notified if the parent is tuning in. And once the ride ends, the live video automatically stops. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Uber says that security and privacy remain a top priority, noting that only the parent or guardian linked to the teen’s account can view live video during an active trip. And the video is encrypted, meaning the driver, guardian, and teen do not have access to the recording after the trip ends. Still, it’s an acknowledgement that many parents may still feel trepidation about letting their teens loose in the world, especially amid ongoing concerns about the safety of ridehail rides. Uber, in particular, is currently facing over 4,000 active sexual assault and misconduct lawsuits filed by passengers in state and federal courts — many of which involve alleged assaults committed by drivers. Uber has said that drivers must maintain top ratings and clean safety records to qualify for teen trips. This isn’t the first time Uber has asked drivers for access to their selfie cameras. If a driver manually turns on the optional Record My Ride feature, the Uber app will use their phone’s front-facing camera and microphone to automatically record trips. And Uber says it can’t view these trip recordings unless the driver chooses to upload and send them when filing a safety report.

articles.title: Our go-to earbuds for taking calls have fallen to their lowest price to date
articles.summary: The Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro have an excellent microphone, impressive ANC, and a charging case with a screen. They’re also on sale for $129.99 for Black Friday.
articles.body: If you’re looking for a new pair of earbuds, the Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro are on sale for $129.99 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart right now. That’s the lowest price we’ve seen for Anker’s excellent wireless earbuds, which normally retail for $169.99 and come in four colors (black, white, blue, and pink) all of which are discounted through November 30th as part of Anker’s ongoing Black Friday promo. [Product: Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro | While the Liberty 5 Pro have a number of great features — including support LDAC for high-res audio and an IP55 dust and water resistance rating — the call quality is what stands out. The microphone does an impressive job cutting out background noise, and my colleague John Higgins praised the Liberty 5 Pro for filtering out emergency vehicles, arborists cutting tree branches, and even loud children. The active noise cancellation is excellent, which helps when you’re trying to hear someone on the other end of the phone whose earbuds aren’t as clear as yours. The charging case also features a handy 0.96-inch screen, so you can adjust the ANC and sound profile on the fly. Read our Anker Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro review.

articles.title: Amazon’s first digital photo frame is up to 50 percent off for Black Friday
articles.summary: The Alexa Photo Frame is on sale starting at $114.99 ($115 off) for Black Friday, which is the first sizable discount we’ve seen on the 10-inch digital frame.
articles.body: Amazon only announced its first digital photo frame less than a month ago, but it’s already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. You can currently grab the Alexa Photo Frame at Amazon and Best Buy starting at $114 ($115 off), making it a great holiday gift for anyone who loves displaying family photos. If you prefer the walnut trim over the birch or standard black models, it’s also on sale at Best Buy for $134.99 ($95 off) — which, like with the others, is the first discount we’ve seen. [Product: Amazon Alexa Photo Frame | The Alexa Photo Frame features a 10-inch, semi-matte touchscreen that’s designed to make digital photos look more natural, with built-in light sensors that automatically adjust brightness throughout the day. It displays images from Amazon Photos, which supports uploads from both iOS and Android devices, including photos stored in iCloud. You can choose which people or albums to display, or let Alexa Plus do the work, which often results in photos based on your facial expression, the season, and even the lighting. You can also search for specific photos with voice commands, letting you easily pull up images of your first dog, your child as a baby, and other shots without having to scroll endlessly through years of photos yourself. If you want to add a more personal touch, Amazon also lets you attach voice notes to individual photos via the Amazon Photos app. For example, you can add a recording of your kid explaining their Halloween costume to a trick-or-treating photo. Plus, you can preload the frame with photos and recordings before gifting it, so your loved one won’t have to spend time setting it up. We’re still testing Amazon’s answer to the Aura frame, but it looks like a particularly good option if you’re already an Amazon Prime member. A Prime subscription grants you unlimited full-resolution photo storage and access to Alexa Plus at no additional cost, and unlike Amazon’s smart displays, the frame doesn’t serve up annoying ads. That said, you don’t need a subscription to use it, and new users can always access a limited-time trial of Alexa Plus.

articles.title: Your questions about Apple HomeView’s audio, answered
articles.summary: We tested the smart display’s sound against a HomePod Mini, put AirPlay and Handoff through their paces, and found third-party apps like Spotify frustrating.
articles.body: After I published my review of the HomeView, Apple’s first smart display, y’all still had a ton of questions about how it works as a smart speaker. So, I spent a bunch more time testing its audio capabilities and support for third-party music apps — and found a few more frustrations along the way. Here are the answers to all your burning questions. Have more? I’ll answer them in the comments. [Image: Clockwise from left: HomeView, HomePod (second-gen), Sonos One, HomePod Mini 2. How does the HomeView sound compared to the HomePod Mini, Sonos One, and HomePod? The HomeView isn’t a replacement for a Sonos One, a full-size HomePod, or a similar-size speaker. Those are much better speakers. In size and sound, the HomeView is closer to the HomePod Mini. I tested it alongside the Mini 2 (which sounds marginally better than the first-gen Mini) and found the tabletop HomeView mostly comparable, with these caveats: The HomeView has better bass and is slightly louder, but it’s not as clear and is less room-filling. You can hear them both in action in this video, alongside the full-size HomePod, the Sonos One, and the wall-mounted HomeView: [Video: Apple HomeView Smart Speaker Audio Testing] The difference comes down to the hardware. The Mini 2 has a single full-range driver and two passive radiators, whereas the tabletop HomeView has two drivers in the display, plus a woofer and two passive radiators in its base. While the woofer adds some oomph, the HomeView’s display, which sits over the speaker base, partly covers it, affecting the sound compared to the Mini. Apple added an accelerometer to the display because tilting it changes the sound, so HomeView adjusts its EQ in real time based on the angle. Still, the Mini, while not as loud, fills a room better, thanks partly to its 360-degree sound. (The HomeView supports Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos, which the Mini 2 doesn’t.) The wall-mounted HomeView has only two drivers, with computational audio Apple says is “tuned specifically for on-wall placement.” It sounds fine but is noticeably thinner than the tabletop version, and bass is basically non-existent. I wouldn’t recommend it for its sound quality, but it’s great for talking to a visitor through your video doorbell. Can you pair two HomeViews for stereo sound? [Image: Two HomeViews can’t be paired for stereo sound, as the HomePod Minis can. I use a stereo pair in my office, and they pack a decent punch in the small space. No. While you can group HomeViews with any other AirPlay speakers to play music out of them all at once, you can’t pair two for a stereo setup or pair a HomeView with a HomePod or Mini. I like the sound of two Minis paired in stereo and use this setup in my office and my bedroom. They also work as speakers for my Apple TVs in those rooms. If you have $300 to spend on a good-sounding smart speaker setup, go with two Minis over a HomeView. The HomeView’s real benefit is the screen. I cover its uses extensively in my full review, but for audio in particular, I like that the screen acts like a jukebox, making it easy to change songs, select new music, and scroll through your podcasts or audiobooks — without needing to find a quarter! With a HomePod, you rely on Siri voice control or your Apple device to select content. [Image: Handoff on HomeView works with audio and video and requires holding the phone near the bottom of the screen. Can you AirPlay music/podcasts to the HomeView, and does audio handoff work? You can AirPlay to the HomeView as with any other AirPlay speaker, and audio handoff works the same as it does on HomePods. Tap your phone to the HomeView, and whatever is playing transfers to the speakers and the screen. Handoff also works in reverse, letting you send any content back to your phone. One addition with the HomeView: You can now hand off video. [Image: Some video apps, including YouTube TV, can use handoff even without an app on the HomeView. In testing, handoff worked for Apple TV, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pocket Casts, YouTube Music, FaceTime, and phone calls — although phone calls sometimes dropped. YouTube and YouTube TV videos also handed off, even though they don’t have an app on the HomeView. But Netflix and Amazon Prime Video only played audio, though both played video in the Safari browser. One word of caution: Handoff is aggressive. As with HomePods, if you’re holding your phone within a few inches, the HomeView will try to hand off content. Can you set a default speaker for the HomeView? [Image: HomeViews can AirPlay audio to HomePods, Apple TVs, and other AirPlay-enabled speakers or devices. HomeView doesn’t let you set a default speaker or group to use instead of its built-in speaker. However, you can play audio to any AirPlay speaker or group of speakers. I tested this on HomePods, Sonos speakers, and a Samsung TV, and it worked smoothly. For native apps (Apple Music, Podcasts, and Safari), the HomeView remembers the last speaker or speaker pair you used and automatically plays content through those when you return. If it’s been a while since you opened the app, it pops up the option to choose the last-used speakers. Things get messier with third-party audio apps such as Spotify and Audible, and with Apple apps that use the CarPlay interface, such as Apple News and Apple TV. The HomeView only automatically uses the last speakers if you choose content from the HomeView screen. If you use Siri voice control, it defaults to the HomeView speaker. So, “Hey Siri, play ‘Femininomenon’ by Chappell Roan from Spotify” played music from HomeView’s speaker and not the stereo pair of Minis in my office, where I’d last been listening to Spotify. I could direct it to play music there by adding “on Office,” but that’s more of a mouthful than just “Hey Siri, play ‘Femininomenon’ by Chappell Roan,” which is all you need to say if you use Apple Music. Which brings me to another one of your most-asked questions — and my biggest complaint about this device as a smart speaker: How does it support third-party audio apps? Like second-class citizens. Does Spotify work on the HomeView? [Image: Audio and video CarPlay apps appear on the HomeView app drawer when your phone is on the same Wi-Fi network, and you have a profile on the device. Spotify works on the HomeView, but with limitations that apply to all non-native and third-party apps: they only show up when your phone is connected to the HomeView via your profile, so only you can use them. Apple has taken a shortcut here: Rather than building a dedicated HomeView experience for app developers, the HomeView uses Apple’s existing CarPlay platform. This makes it easier for developers to put their apps on the HomeView — if an audio or video app supports CarPlay, it already works on the HomeView (there’s no support for other types of CarPlay apps). In practice, this creates frustrating limitations, including no search function and the need for a user profile on the HomeView and your phone on the same Wi-Fi. It also results in slower performance and a laggy, inconsistent experience compared to the native apps. I tried several apps: Pocket Casts, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, Spotify, and Audible. They all appeared in my HomeView app drawer, and I could access them, choose content via streamlined interfaces, and then play audio on the HomeView or AirPlay from it to any speakers. But CarPlay apps don’t work as well as the built-in audio apps — Music, Podcasts, and Safari. They take longer to load and respond more slowly. You also can’t type a search query in any of them, as you can in the native apps, because they don’t have a search field or keyboard. Instead, you have to scroll through content to find what you want or use Siri voice search. There’s no search box because you’re not supposed to type while driving; only I’m not driving — I’m in my kitchen! This shows how much of a CarPlay port the apps are; they haven’t been updated to account for the fact that this device is stationary and in your home. Case in point, when I first pulled up the Apple TV app (the only CarPlay video app currently supported), a warning popped up telling me to make sure I was stationary before watching any video. Playing audio through CarPlay apps is also buggy. It didn’t always bring up the music control screen, so I had to use my iPhone to control it. Plus, the Audible app often refused to load at all and didn’t work with Siri voice search. Me: “Siri, resume my Audible book.” Siri: “Shuffling latest songs from Apple Music.” CarPlay support feels like a stopgap, and Apple needs to work with developers to refine the software and add HomeView-specific controls for a better, more integrated experience. [Image: A smart display has several functions beyond being a smart speaker. One feature I like on the HomeView is its guided cooking experience. Should you buy a HomeView as a smart speaker? Much of the confusion around the HomeView stems from treating it like a smart speaker when it’s really a smart display. I get it; I’ve spent the last decade frustrated by smart displays from Google and Amazon that promise a lot but rarely do it all well. [Product: Apple HomeView | If you don’t care about the other features of a smart display and just want a smart speaker, then the reason to buy a HomeView over a HomePod is if you have a use for it as a touchscreen music controller. This lets anyone in the household easily browse and control what’s playing. Bear in mind, though, Apple Music (with a subscription) is the only app anyone can use to play music on the HomeView, as CarPlay apps require a user profile. [Product: Apple HomePod Mini 2 | If you want a smart speaker primarily to play music and are happy using your voice or phone to control it, go for a HomePod. If you use Spotify or other third-party music services, consider an Echo Dot or Google Home smart speaker; both let you set a default speaker and a default music provider — such as Spotify. If you already own HomePods and use Apple Music, the HomeView’s touchscreen will fit in nicely as a simple way to control audio. Just don’t buy one expecting it to fully replace a dedicated smart speaker.

articles.title: How Tamagotchis got us hooked on digital pets
articles.summary: On Version History: Why millions of people signed up to feed, change, and play with a beeping little keychain.
articles.body: If you were are a kid in the late 1990s, there’s a near-100 percent chance you either had a Tamagotchi or knew someone who did. The tiny digital pets came out of nowhere and became an overnight sensation, as millions of kids signed up to parent a crying, hungry, constantly dirty creature. Until they went to school, anyway, at which point their parents were given some new responsibilities they neither asked for nor wanted. On this episode of Version History, we dig deep into the story of the Tamagotchi. That story has its 30th anniversary this week, even though the real craze only lasted a few years. David Pierce is joined by The Verge’s Mia Sato and Victoria Song to discuss the origins of the Tamagotchi, the product’s many iterations, its incredible engagement tactics, and whether any of us could tolerate the Tama experience three decades later. (We… could not.) This is the second episode of the sixth season of Version History, all about tech for your pets — and tech that is pets. Last week we fell back in love with the Sony Aibo, and there’s lots more to come this season. f you want to be sure not to miss anything, there are a few ways to subscribe: * The Version History podcast feed * The Version History YouTube channel * Our TikTok and Instagram accounts If you’re a Verge subscriber, you can also get access to Version History (and all our other podcasts) with no ads. All you have to do is visit your account settings. If you want to know more about the Tamagotchi, here are some links to get you started: * From The New York Times in 1997: The Tamagotchi: Toy Life-Form Invades the U.S. * From Smithsonian: A Brief History of Tamagotchi * From RetroDodo: The CRAZY History Of Tamagotchi * From BBC World Service: Witness History, Tamagotchi is born * The AI Tamagotchis are coming

articles.title: ‘The show is starting soon. Please turn on your headphones.’
articles.summary: Off-Broadway show Love Me uses Auracast Bluetooth technology both for accessibility and as a part of its sound design.
articles.body: Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse. As we filter to our seats, ushers hand each person a black drawstring bag with a pair of wired headphones connected to a small Auracast receiver. Then, soon after the play begins, we’re instructed to put them on. The headphones are an integral storytelling tool of Love Me — a one-man show from the minds of stand-up comedian and former Saturday Night Live writer Drew Michael and director Prashanth Venkataramanujam. It’s a show about love and the bid for connection, told in five chapters about different relationships in Michael’s life, bound by the threads of his hearing loss and self-discovery. Love Me’s experimental sound design is possible thanks to Auracast, a technology based on Bluetooth that can broadcast a high-quality audio stream to any number of nearby devices. As the show follows Michael from childhood through adulthood, sound designer Daniel Kluger uses the headphones in combination with the theater speakers to create experiences that wouldn’t be possible with a traditional setup. Tinnitus ringing and hearing test tones play in the music between sections as subtle clues as the show builds to Michael’s epiphany about his hearing loss. Kluger also explores the world through varying levels of sonic clarity. Sound playing through the theater’s speakers is sometimes intentionally muffled, which is then further dulled by the headphones, giving the audience a sense of what Michael is hearing in those moments. But one sound that stays clear and pristine is Michael’s inner monologue, heard in the headphones throughout the show. The inner monologue consists of both prerecorded tracks and the live feed from Michael’s microphone on stage as he talks back and forth with himself. “Any time you’re in my head — anything in the headphones is coming through clearly,” Michael tells me after the show. “[We’re] trying to also highlight that the appeal of the inner world is such that it’s the highest fidelity space for this person. It’s more comfortable.” The different sound sources and treatments of the sound can lead to intentionally confusing scenes for the audience. During one, where Michael is doing a stand-up set at a comedy club, three sounds compete for attention: The theater speakers play the crowd’s reactions (including a heckler whose voice is sometimes muffled and sometimes clear); his prerecorded inner monologue reacting to the crowd plays in the headphones; and on stage, Michael is performing the set, with his mic muffled so our focus is on his inner monologue. It’s one of the definitive moments where the audience feels the constant concentration necessary to parse what’s happening when sounds aren’t clear and become overwhelming. [Image: [Image: But the biggest impact comes during a climactic scene the sound design has been building toward, a realization that also incorporates the visuals of a series of Michael’s audiograms over the years. “I had this massive breakthrough about the whole history of what I’ve been doing — the cognitive labor, the invisible to myself labor that was affecting every single minute of my life,” Michael says. “That was a huge moment.” That’s when the audience is instructed to remove the headphones we’ve been wearing for nearly the entire show. As Michael comes to the recognition of his relationship with his hearing loss and the clarity of mind that gives him, what we’ve become used to for the entire show’s experience — the headphones — are now gone, as is that literal weight from our heads. It’s an emotional moment, one that I’ve thought about multiple times since seeing the show. It also leads into the final act, where Michael begins to understand his own Deaf identity. “The deafness is not the culprit, it’s the denial of it.” he tells me. “My hearing currently has never been worse, but I’ve never been more self-affirmed or self-actualized or felt happier in myself. It’s a misconception, I think, about deafness as a tragedy, deafness as a deficit, deafness as a burden, deafness as something that plagues a person.” The ability of Auracast to broadcast an audio stream that any number of headphones can connect to is what made Love Me a possibility. Any Auracast headphones can connect to the audience broadcast — I brought along the Nothing Pro 1 to test the ability and connected to the audience broadcast channel in seconds — but I used the provided Auri receiver and Austrian Audio headset for the performance. The show’s sound was designed with those in mind, and I didn’t want the differing isolation of the Nothing headphones to affect the intent of the experience. [Image: [Image: Love Me is presented in partnership with Deaf West Theatre, which supports Deaf-centered storytelling in theatrical productions. In addition to the audience Auracast feed, there’s one for users of hearing aids and cochlear implants that’s designed for compliance with those devices, and iPads with captions are also available. During the performance, Michael connects to his own broadcast channel with Auracast-enabled Phonak Eon Sphere hearing aids. “We talked about using in-ear monitors, but if I use an in-ear monitor, then I don’t have amplification from my environment, so then I lose contact with the audience,” Michael says. “These function as two things: They’re hearing aids and also in-ear monitors.” Love Me relies on the Auracast technology to tell its story, but it isn’t a story about hearing technology. The technology is there to tell the story of connection and discovery of identity. “I think right now … there are two things that are at odds — the hearing aid and audiological tech side of deafness and then the cultural identity side of deafness,” Michael says. Technological improvements, like cochlear implants and hearing aids, are cited as one of the reasons schools for the deaf have been on the decline, which leads to kids being mainstreamed (put into regular public schools) and losing out on Deaf history and culture. “I’m not against the tech,” Michael says, “I just think tech and Deaf identity should be a marriage rather than a divide.” And that collaboration is why Love Me works as well as it does. The Auracast technology is there both for accessibility — in the same way it’s already used in other performances, lectures, or announcement systems — and to uplift the show’s story of love, acceptance, and acknowledgement of one’s own Deaf identity. It’s an inventive use of the technology that carries with it a powerful message.

articles.title: Nintendo’s Switch 2 console is $50 off for Black Friday
articles.summary: Following a $50 price increase in September, Nintendo has knocked that amount off the its Mario Kart World Switch 2 bundle, making it a great Black Friday deal.
articles.body: Those hoping to save some cash on a Nintendo Switch 2 can do so starting today, November 22nd, through Saturday, December 5th, giving you plenty of time to think about it after Cyber Monday has passed. For a limited time, Nintendo has knocked $50 off one of its two current console bundles, temporarily rolling back the $50 price increase that went into effect in early September. It’s tough to predict which bundle will be most popular for your household. The Mario Kart World bundle runs $499.99 (previously $549.99) and includes the console, a digital copy of the aforementioned game, and three months of Nintendo Switch Online. Then there’s the Nintendo Switch Sports Resort bundle for $529.99 (price unchanged for Black Friday), which includes the more recent minigame-filled title instead. Both are currently available from Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Nintendo. [Product: Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle | Nintendo has delivered hit after hit since the console launched in mid-2025. There are now plenty of excellent games to justify snagging a Switch 2, including, most recently, the stellar remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Plus, the newer console can play nearly all of the original Switch games, and it’s wirelessly compatible with the older system’s Joy-Con and Switch Pro controllers. If you’re planning to get a Switch 2, below are some useful guides filled with accessory recommendations. From tempered glass screen protectors and protective cases to controllers, there are plenty of goodies that’ll help you take better care of your Switch 2 and get more enjoyment from it.

articles.title: Can a TV be too large? An investigation
articles.summary: Can a TV be too large? This writer's recent upgrade to a 65-inch OLED came with some unexpected challenges.
articles.body:
For the past couple of years, I’ve wanted to upgrade my home entertainment situation from the humble trappings of my long sufficient 55-inch TCL smart TV to the model much coveted by cinephiles the world over: the OLED.

The organic light-emitting diode is a specific monitor technology that has really changed the TV industry. Unlike an LED TV, which creates images by shining a backlight through a panel of pixels, OLEDs leverage millions of self-lighting pixels, which provides significantly better pixel control, and can generate a much more nuanced image with deeply vibrant colors and a more intense light and shadows.

They are also significantly more expensive, which is one reason that I’ve held off on investing in one for years. However, this year I couldn’t wait any longer. I finally sprang for an upgrade and, since I was already upgrading on image quality, I decided to upgrade the size, too: I bought a 65-inch LG evo C4, which is the company’s mid-range unit released in 2024.

At first, the experience was amazing. The television rendered colors and shadows wonderfully and, seeing as one of the goals with this purchase was to indulge my physical media habit, I began running through my collection of 4K Blu-ray discs with the madcap energy of a true fanatic.

However, things took a bit of an unexpected turn when, midway through “McCabe and Mrs. Miller,” I was suddenly overcome by a wave of nausea. I’m not particularly sensitive to motion sickness, but this sensation — which made it feel vaguely like I was going to hurl — persisted for several hours after it initially began. It was then replaced by a small tension headache.

I discovered that this is actually a somewhat common experience for new OLED adopters. Indeed, Reddit is rife with posts from new television owners who claim they feel like their big new toy is breaking their brain.

“I got the tv yesterday and still feel sick today,” one Redditor , who said they had recently purchased an LG C2, wrote. “Feel light headed and nauseous a day later. Thinking about taking it back. Is this normal? I’m scared to turn the thing on lol.”

Others blamed the sheer size of the screen. One guy, who bought an 85-inch TLC, claimed it had led his wife to the conclusion that “it’s too big and say that she feels sick watching. Is that a thing that a screen can be too big?”

There doesn’t seem to be a consensus on why this happens. Many Redditors blame certain motion-smoothing settings. However, my TV did not come with those settings enabled. Others blamed viewers for sitting too close to the screen — yet I was sitting a solid nine feet away, which is well within the recommended range for a 65-inch screen.

Finally, others have argued that the screen brightness could be agitating users’ eyes. I dialed down the brightness on mine to around 50 percent, although I had doubts as to whether this actually had anything to do with the feelings I was having.

In considering my nausea, one theory that sprang to mind was that it might just be my eyes’ inexperience with viewing such a big screen. The TV was so large that it often felt like my eye had to trace different parts of the screen to take in the whole picture and, if the scene involved significant motion (most movie scenes do, after all), it conjured the sensation of trying to stare too intently at something out the window of a moving car.

After a few days, however, my eyes finally adjusted. The nausea was gone. All that remained was an immense and beautiful home viewing experience that made every previous viewing experience pale by comparison.

Initial physiological reactions aside, the size of the 65-inch screen (and whether your living space actually has room for it) is still something that needs to be considered carefully by potential buyers. I recently moved into a place with a slightly bigger living room, which has given me the flexibility to install a bigger device. At my old apartment, however, this size of TV would have definitely felt like it was devouring the space.

Another slight frustration is that the C4 does not come with any detailed installation instructions. The screen (which is so wide it’s difficult to move without another person there to help you) comes detached from its base, and the user is just sort of expected to figure out how to effectively move and put together the two pieces. A quick YouTube video is all that is necessary to understand this process, but you have to be careful when moving and assembling the pieces so as not to scratch or damage the screen.

Once the whole thing is set up and assembled, the OLED is a truly beautiful thing to behold. The customization that’s possible, including advanced brightness and color control — and things like “Filmmaker Mode” (which claims to adjust each movie’s color and frame rate settings to those intended by the director) — make the user experience really powerful.

To sum up: The evo C4 is a really spectacular piece of equipment that has a lot to offer the avid home entertainment viewer — although there may be a bit of a learning curve before it makes your cinema dreams come true.

articles.title: Siri AI settlement could pay out $61 per iPhone.
articles.summary:
Apple agreed to settle the class action suit in May, and iPhone owners could start submitting claims in September. With the December 21st deadline for claims approaching, lawyers have a better idea of how much each claimant should receive. According to MacRumors:
> The exact payment amount per eligible iPhone will depend on the total number of valid claims submitted and other factors, up to a maximum of $95. The lawyers representing the class members expect payouts of at least $61 per eligible iPhone, unless there is a significant uptick in claims submitted.
articles.body: Apple agreed to settle the class action suit in May, and iPhone owners could start submitting claims in September. With the December 21st deadline for claims approaching, lawyers have a better idea of how much each claimant should receive. articles.title: Delta flights in and out of Atlanta delayed due to system outage
articles.summary: Major delays for Delta come just a week after a nationwide groundstop.
articles.body: All Delta flights in and out of Atlanta are facing significant delays on Sunday due to a problem with the system that calculates a plane’s weight and balance. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is Delta’s largest hub and one of the busiest airports in the world. While only Delta is impacted at the moment, disruptions at Hartsfield-Jackson could potentially affect other airports and airlines if delays continue to pile up. The issues with Delta’s systems in Atlanta come just one week after an FAA outage led to a nationwide groundstop and thousands of canceled flights. According to The New York Times: > The system that went offline calculates the total weight of an airplane, including its airframe, fuel, passengers and their baggage. The system also allows pilots to determine the plane’s center of gravity and whether the weight is evenly distributed — data points that help ensure safe passage. > “Delta teams are using manual workarounds this morning to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” the airline said in a statement on Sunday.

articles.title: The best apps to make new friends right now | TechCrunch
articles.summary: We've compiled a list of friendship apps, from friend discovery platforms like BFF to event-focused ones like Timeleft.
articles.body:
In recent years, people have been increasingly looking for new ways to form platonic connections, as loneliness and social isolation have become more prevalent.

In 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General went so far as to label this issue a public health crisis. Remote workers, who miss the everyday interactions found in an office, and younger individuals eager to create their adult social circles based on shared interests and hobbies, are among those seeking meaningful friendships.

Thanks to online dating apps, the stigma associated with finding connections online has largely faded away. This has welcomed a new wave of apps focused on fostering friendships and building local communities.

According to estimates from Appfigures, over a dozen local-focused friendship apps have collectively generated approximately $16 million in consumer spending in the U.S. so far this year. Some notable examples include Timeleft, Meet5, and Bumble’s BFF. Additionally, these apps have garnered approximately 4.3 million downloads thus far in 2025.

The apps aim to provide a less awkward solution than, for instance, approaching a stranger at the gym or local café and trying to strike up a conversation. These platforms clearly indicate that everyone using the app is looking for the same thing — friendship, not romance — making it much less intimidating to initiate conversations.

From major players like Meetup to newer ones like 222, there are plenty of apps that cater to the growing demand for meaningful friendships. We’ve compiled a list of them for you to try out.

The app 222 is an iOS-only social events platform that facilitates in-person meetups by pairing a group of strangers based on their personality test results. The app sends invitations to nearby public social events, such as wine bars and comedy clubs. There is then a vetting process, and selected participants are notified on the day of the event. A bonus for those who feel socially anxious: You’re allowed to bring a plus-one.

The service charges a $22.22 curation fee or a monthly subscription for the same price.

Dating giant Bumble is among the more established players to enter the friendship space, launching its friend-finding feature in 2016, which then spun out into a stand-alone app in 2023. The friend-making app has recently undergone a significant redesign , with an increased emphasis on facilitating group meetups, catering to users’ desires to grow their social circles.

BFF is available for free download on iOS and Android devices.

Clyx is another emerging app in the group-based social networking landscape, with a strong focus on discovering local events. The social platform helps users find community events by integrating data from platforms like Ticketmaster and TikTok. Additionally, Clyx allows users to upload their contact lists, helping them see which events their friends plan to attend. The app also includes a feature that recommends other users to connect with at these events.

As of now, Clyx operates exclusively in two cities: Miami and London. However, it has plans to expand to additional areas in the near future, with New York City and São Paulo at the top of the list. The app is available on the App Store and Google Play Store .

Crowdier is a new group social app that lets friend groups connect with others. Users can create a group of 2-5 friends and browse other groups to arrange hangouts in person.

To initiate a match, users can “Wave” at groups they like, and if those groups wave back, they can plan in a shared chat. A match requires the majority of both groups to agree. For example, 2 people in a 4-person group needs to say yes.

The app is available for free on iOS and Android devices.

Les Amís is a friendship app tailored for women, transgender, and LGBTQ+ individuals that leverages AI to match users based on similar interests and encourages participation in local events, such as pottery classes, book clubs, and wine tastings. Matches are made every Monday, allowing users to chat and plan meetups later in the week.

Available on iOS and Android , Les Amís serves cities across Europe, including Amsterdam, Barcelona, Berlin, Madrid, Paris, and Stockholm. In the U.S., the app is available in Austin and New York, with plans to expand to Boston, Miami, and Los Angeles.

The app uses a paid membership model that varies by city, with fees of $70 in New York and €55 in Amsterdam.

The local event-discovery platform has been around since 2002, helping millions of users connect with others who share similar interests. Users can RSVP to events; join groups that cater to a variety of hobbies, professions, or social causes; and create their own groups and events. They can also chat with group members and post updates and photos from gatherings.

This European community-building app recently launched in the U.S., targeting users over 40 who want to meet new people in their area and participate in group activities such as picnics, concerts, and hiking. Notably, in a short time, there have been around 777,000 U.S. downloads so far across the App Store and Google Play Store , according to Appfigures estimates.

Pie is another one of the newer social apps on the market. It features an AI-driven quiz designed to predict which users are most likely to be compatible with each other. Each person who RSVPs to a Pie event takes a brief personality assessment, and the algorithm organizes attendees into groups of six, who are then added to a group chat within the Pie app, allowing them to interact with each other before the event.

Currently, the app is only available in Austin, Chicago, and San Francisco. Users can download Pie from the App Store and Google Play Store .

Timeleft is a relatively new platform that helps you organize weekly dinner dates with groups of strangers. The app uses a special algorithm to match you with others, taking into account your age, gender, and personality. Users are matched with four other people, but they only learn minor details about them the night before, including their occupations and zodiac signs.

Dinners take place at a selected restaurant on Wednesday evenings at 7:00 p.m. To help everyone break the ice, the app offers a game with conversation starters. After dinner, there is an after-party at a local bar.

Users can book dinners online or through the app . In terms of pricing, it varies depending on the country and restaurant. Users pay for a ticket up front and are responsible for covering their own dinner and drinks.

Washed Up is a social event discovery app that launched in early 2026, designed for people in the Los Angeles area who want an easier way to find things to do and meet new people.

The app helps users discover local events, such as concerts, trivia nights, and comedy shows, while also giving them a built-in way to connect with others who plan to attend. Instead of going to events alone, users can create or join “plans,” which are small group meetups tied to specific events. Users can browse these plans and request to join, chat with the group, and add new friends, making it easier to show up to events with people rather than by themselves.

It’s available to download on the App Store .

Wyzr Friends is an activity-based friendship app designed for adults 40 and older, catering to empty nesters, those who are divorced, and other users seeking to connect with like-minded individuals. Users can thumbs up or down potential friends and arrange in-person activities based on shared interests, such as going to the movies or hiking.

It’s available on iOS and Android devices in the U.S., Canada, Australia, Ireland, the Philippines, Singapore, and Mexico.

Mmotion is a newly launched friendship app that blends location tracking with social discovery to help users connect with people nearby and explore new bars and restaurants in their area. Upon joining, users can participate in interest-based groups — such as hiking, basketball, or art — view a map of active users, and send messages to those nearby. The app also highlights new places on the map, making it easy to find a restaurant or venue to try.

Mmotion is currently only available to users in New York City on iOS and Android devices. Users must first submit an application to be considered.

Launched in March 2026, Synchrony is a new social app tailored for neurodivergent adults. Founded by a mother of a son on the autism spectrum, it aims to create a supportive community through features like interest-based matching and two-step identity verification. This ensures that users engage safely, as both a user and a trusted person must verify personal details and a photo ID during registration.

A standout feature is Jesse, an optional AI communication tool that assists users in navigating conversations. The AI provides editable prompts to help express thoughts, clarifies conversations, and offers boundary-setting suggestions. While the incorporation of AI may raise concerns, there are guardrails built into Jesse, such as avoiding medical advice.

Users must pay a monthly subscription of $44.99 after a 30-day free trial. It’s available on iOS and Android devices.

This story was updated after publication.

articles.title: 'Dancing with the Stars’ alum John O’Hurley talks about his weight loss journey: 'I lost 25 lbs, I was in the best shape of my life, but…’
articles.summary: John O'Hurley shares his weight loss journey from 'Dancing with the Stars', discussing his experience with dancing, losing 25 lbs, and competing for the Mirrorball Trophy.
articles.body: TV presenter and actor John O’Hurley, who appeared on the famed ‘Dancing with the Stars’ show back in 2005, recently looked back on his time on the show. O’Hurley opened up about how, at the time, it was one of the hardest things he'd ever done and that he lost quite a lot of weight for the inaugural season. Read ahead to learn more about what he had to share.John O’Hurley talks about losing weight for ‘Dancing with the Stars'O’Hurley was paired with Charlotte Jørgensen as the two rose in the ranks on the first season of ‘DWTS.’ While talking to PEOPLE about his time on the show and while he and his partner were competing for the Mirrorball Trophy, he admitted that the show took quite a toll on his body.“I lost 25 lbs., so I was in the best shape of my life. But it was seven hours a day, seven days a week. It was difficult. It really was," he revealed during the interview. The star also shared, “I was good at the smooth styles, the foxtrot, and the waltz, and I was terrible at everything that ended in a vowel. All the Latin dances. But if it ended in a vowel, I was terrible at it. And I do remember Bruno [Tonioli] was going, ‘You’ve got to move your hips!'"He also commented on how the show's system meant that if you did well enough for one week, you could return for the next week with something completely new. O’Hurley and Jørgensen made it to the finals to win the Mirrorball Trophy; however, their journey ended in the finale after they were eliminated from the final run.Recalling his time on the show, O’Hurley joked a lot and even commented, “The carrot was always being held farther and farther from me each week, but it was a wonderful time.”John O’Hurley shares that he did not know how to dance at all once he entered the showDuring the same interview, the ‘Seifield’ cast member shared that he was not aware of any dance moves at all, and at that time he had been cast along with Charlotte Jørgensen, who was, at the time, one of the number one ballroom dancers in the world. She continued, “I had no experience at all. So fortunately, I had Charlotte Jørgensen as my partner, and she was the No. 1 ballroom dancer in the world at the time. So I learned a lot from her, and we made ourselves pretty competitive.”They lost the show to Kelly Monaco and her partner, Alec Mazo. However, soon after, due to public demand, Hurley was allowed to dance with Charlotte Jørgensen against Monaco and her partner in a ‘grudge’ face-off, which landed Charlotte and O’Hurley in the lead, making her the winner. The two ended up winning the second match and landed their big prize money and the Mirrorball Trophy.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kodak’s next collectible is a tiny digital photo frame that doubles as a tracker
articles.summary: The Kodak SlideTag is a keychain-sized digital photo frame featuring a low-power color E Ink screen and tracking capabilities using Google’s and Apple’s networks.
articles.body: After expanding its Charmera collection with a Millennium Edition featuring Y2K-inspired designs earlier this year, Reto’s follow-up to its tiny Kodak camera is an equally small digital photo frame you can use to display your shots. But while the Charmera’s usefulness stopped at snapping grainy photos and terrible videos, the Kodak SlideTag goes one step further. It also functions as a Bluetooth tracker that’s compatible with either Apple’s Find My or Google’s Find Hub tracking networks. The Kodak SlideTag will be available for $34.99 each and, like the Charmera, will feature a series of retro designs distributed in mystery boxes so you don’t know which one you’re going to get. Reto also sells a complete set of all eight vintage designs for $279.92 if you don’t like mysteries; however, there’s a ninth “secret edition” only available in the individual boxes with a sleek metallic finish. [Image: The SlideTag is a bit smaller than a classic Kodak film slide, but far more functional and versatile. For those who grew up in an era where projectors are small enough to integrate into phones, the SlideTag is designed to look like a modernized version of the film slides that were used to project photos decades ago. Instead of film, the SlideTag features a 1.54-inch color E Ink screen that mixes six colored inks to display photos at a resolution of 240 x 240. [Image: Illustrations with bold, defined colors will translate best to the SlideTag’s color E Ink screen. The color reproduction won’t be as accurate as an LCD or OLED screen, but the SlideTag can hold and cycle up to 12 photos transferred to the device over Bluetooth from Kodak’s Memory Link app running on a mobile device. You can also use it to display a short to-do list, contact details, a countdown timer, or a QR code linking to wherever you want. As a tracker it’s not quite as functional as an Apple AirTag or Google’s Pixel Tag, which use features like ultra wideband (UWB) and Channel Sounding to make them easier to find. The SlideTag sticks to basic Bluetooth with a range of up to 30 meters out in the open and a 75-decibel buzzer to help locate it when you’re close. Battery life will vary depending on how frequently you use tracking features or refresh the displayed image, but the SlideTag uses a common CR2032 coin cell battery that’s easy to replace.

articles.title: New report further 'confirms' Alice Huang as Chinese spy during her affair with Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Alice Huang reportedly kept in touch with a Chinese intelligence officer during her affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
articles.body: Alice Huang reportedly kept in touch with a Chinese intelligence officer during her affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The New York Times has reported that her contact with a Chinese spy lasted more than a year. The publication cited people familiar with intelligence reports that described Alice Huang’s encounters with an officer from China’s Ministry of State Security between spring 2025 and fall 2026.The report adds a timeline to the contacts as US authorities investigate Huang and the Singapore-based company she previously led. Attorney General Todd Blanche said this month that the Justice Department had yet to determine whether she had spied for China. US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton addressed the inquiry on CNN’s recent “State of the Union”. He said: “Attorney General Blanche has been very clear that this is a matter under investigation, both Ms Huang and her company, for various matters. And I'm going to let that investigation play out.”Why Megaspeed is part of the investigationAlice Huang ran Megaspeed International, a Singapore firm that once accounted for billions of dollars in Nvidia chip sales. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over allegations it smuggled advanced artificial intelligence-enabled chips from US firm Nvidia to ChinaNYT first reported on the case on October 29. About two weeks later, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had stepped down as president, CEO and a member of its board, effective immediately. The company named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO.Lawmakers question how the US enforces chip restrictionsThe scandal has drawn attention in Washington to export controls, the rules that restrict which advanced chips can be sold to China. Lawmakers from both parties have questioned whether the Trump administration has done enough to enforce those rules.In a November 11 letter, Democratic senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the administration to preserve records concerning the suspected intelligence operation. Their request covered intelligence assessments, briefings and other materials related to Alice Huang, Jensen Huang, Megaspeed and its affiliates.Louisiana Republican Senator John Kennedy indicated on NBC’s “Meet the Press” that he was less interested in the affair itself. “I hope he had a good time,” Kennedy said last week. “It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy.”​Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: Amazon is taking orders for the Moto Tag 3 before it’s even been announced
articles.summary: Motorola’s unannounced Moto Tag 3 has been listed for sale online, just five months after the Moto Tag 2 went on sale in the US.
articles.body: Motorola’s unannounced Moto Tag 3 has been listed for sale online, just five months after the Moto Tag 2 went on sale in the US, and before any official announcement of a follow-up. The listing on Amazon UK was spotted by X user @matteventu, and shows the tracker in a “Pantone Lucent White” color option, with a price of £24.96 (about $33) and a 1-4 month shipping estimate. A second image shared by leaker Evan Blass also shows a vibrant purple version of the new tracking tag, which is described as “Pantone Indigo Blue” on a separate Amazon Italy listing. Both are new color options, with the Moto Tag 2 only currently available in orange or a grey-ish beige. While the Moto Tag 3 name suggests this is a follow-up to the Moto Tag 2, there don’t appear to be any major hardware differences between the two trackers. Both use a replaceable CR2032 battery, claim to provide more than 500 days of battery life, and support UWB in Android Find Hub, among other similarities. The XT2561-1 model number seen on the back of the Moto Tag 3 images also matches that of the Moto Tag 2. That could mean that the Moto Tag 3 name is an error and these are just new color options for the Tag 2. We’ve asked Motorola for clarification and will update if we hear back.

articles.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia’s board has voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO.
articles.body: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA.” In its statement, the board says that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Donald Trump responded to the board’s decision in a post on Truth Social, saying Nvidia “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” The board’s statement says that its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot will continue, with Huang’s support and cooperation, while interim CEO Colette Kress will continue as CFO, and Harvey Jones will remain as the recently appointed board chair. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO. Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including an executive who reported to him. In the wake of his departure, more than 200,000 people, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed a letter to Nvidia’s board, calling for his reinstatement. articles.title: Tesla’s FSD v15 turns driving visuals into Grand Theft Auto
articles.summary: Tesla has started rolling out Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v15, featuring a GTA-like generative “Reality View”, Bike Rack Mode, and speed camera slowdowns amid ongoing NHTSA safety probes.
articles.body: Tesla has begun rolling out Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v15, calling it a ground-up overhaul of its end-to-end driver assist system. The centerpiece is Reality View, a real-time generative display that swaps out old wireframe graphics for a live, overhead camera angle that lets drivers see and tap to influence what the car plans to do next. The third-person perspective renders buildings, crosswalks, pedestrians, and surrounding traffic with a photorealism that has drawn immediate comparisons to Grand Theft Auto VI (which conveniently launched just days earlier). Even Elon Musk couldn’t resist the comparison on X, posting “FSD is GTA irl” shortly after the update dropped on Saturday. Under the hood, FSD v15 runs on an upgraded vision encoder shared across Tesla’s FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus humanoid robot programs. By training the model on millions of online videos, Tesla claims its AI learned to prevent serious driving mistakes 25 times more often while using less computing power. Of course, the update is built for vehicles running Tesla’s newer AI4 (HW4) hardware and upcoming Cybercab platforms, leaving millions of older HW3-equipped cars behind. [Media: Beyond the flashy visuals, v15 packs several practical upgrades. A new Bike Rack Mode lets drivers engage FSD even with hitch accessories attached (though it disables reversing, Summon, and Autopark). The system can now automatically ease off the speed near traffic cameras, with an option to override and permanently mute specific cameras after two cancellations. Tesla also promises sharper hazard avoidance for potholes, standing water, and small animals, alongside smoother speed handling in school zones and bad weather. Meanwhile, navigation learns preferred neighborhood routes and favorite parking spots over time, and the cabin camera can now track driver attention through hats and sunglasses while dialing back nagging alerts at higher speeds. Tesla has a pretty poor reputation for ensuring its drivers stay alert while using FSD, so hopefully this upgrade can improve that. [Media: Still, Reality View raises an obvious question: is a hyper-detailed, video-game-style feed on the center touchscreen a helpful window into the car’s “brain,” or a tempting new distraction? For drivers who find the live feed overwhelming, Tesla includes a map-only option and a stripped-back “quiet mode”. Tesla’s bold “25x” safety claim also lands amid intense federal scrutiny. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is actively investigating roughly 2.9 million FSD-equipped vehicles over reports of Teslas blowing through red lights, crossing railroad tracks improperly, and driving into oncoming lanes. Alongside dozens of cumulative fatalities linked to Tesla’s driver-assistance systems since 2019, the probe is a stark reminder of the gap between Tesla’s autonomous ambitions and a system that still legally requires a human to keep their eyes on the road.

articles.title: The Verge’s favorite holiday gifts that cost $50 or less
articles.summary: We’ve compiled some of our staff’s favorite gifts that are meaningful and useful, from phone accessories to great albums and movies.
articles.body: You’ve got $50 to spend on a friend or loved one this shopping season, and you’re not sure what to spend it on. First off, that’s actually really generous of you. While this price tier can sometimes be challenging to shop for — caught between affordable accessories and big-ticket items — there’s plenty of gold to be mined for clever shoppers. And we’re here to help. articles.title: Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 are a whopping $100 off ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: The AirPods Pro 3 wireless earbuds with noise cancellation and great sound are down to $149.99 at Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart.
articles.body: The AirPods Pro 3 are cheaper than ever. Apple’s latest flagship wireless earbuds dropped this morning to just $149 at Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart. Originally, they sold for $249, but have been commonly available for $199 outside the range of deal events. The best price that we’ve previously seen was $169, which is what they’re currently selling for at Best Buy. It’s a weird situation that, right now, the feature-packed AirPods Pro 3 are the same price as the newer (but less impressive) AirPods 5 that include the wireless charging case. The Pro 3 deliver considerably more bang for your buck. [Product: AirPods Pro 3 | This model is Apple’s best-sounding, longest-lasting AirPods, and they ship with five silicone ear tips. Compared to the second-gen AirPod Pro, these offer better water resistance (IP57 versus IP54), longer battery life per charge (eight hours versus six), improved noise cancellation, and heart rate sensing through built-in sensors. The case also has Apple’s second-gen Ultra Wideband chip in the case. Read our AirPods Pro 3 review.

articles.title: Everyone’s recording each other, Uber edition.
articles.summary:
The ridehail company said today its testing a new “Recorded Rides” feature that lets customers specifically request a trip with a driver who’s recording using Uber’s in-app Record my Ride feature, claiming riders and drivers feel “peace of mind” knowing there’s a record of their trip. Given that Uber is facing over 4,500 federal lawsuits from passengers alleging the company failed to prevent sexual assaults, perhaps that’s true. The feature will roll out first in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis, and St. Louis.

articles.title: My trusty 27-inch Alienware QD-OLED gaming monitor is just $280
articles.summary: The AW2726DM is a fantastic 27-inch 1440p 240Hz gaming monitor, and you can get it at Best Buy and Dell for $279.99, its lowest price yet.
articles.body: Alienware’s AW2726DM QD-OLED gaming monitor was a great deal even at its original $349.99 price. The low price and impressive specs were enough to convince me to get one at launch, and I’m glad that I did. I’m a little jealous that you have the opportunity to save $70 on the monitor I’ve been using for work and play for several months. Best Buy and Dell are selling the 27-inch 1440p monitor for $279.99 ahead of Black Friday. [Product: Alienware AW2726DM QD-OLED monitor | The AW2726DM has more features than other similarly-priced monitors that I was comparing it to, and that still holds true when comparing it to more modern models. It has a 1440p QD-OLED screen that delivers tremendous contrast and deep blacks, and its 240Hz refresh rate provides a high ceiling for my graphics card to deliver fast frames. It’s equipped with HDMI and DisplayPort inputs, and really one of its only flaws is that it lacks USB-C video support. The monitor works great for PC games, as well as console titles. I think it’d be a sweet gift to yourself or to a gamer in your life this holiday. Read my Alienware AW2726DM hands-on.

articles.title: Peacock subscriptions are up to 66 percent off for Black Friday
articles.summary: Thanks to an ongoing Black Friday deal, new and returning subscribers can sign up for a Peacock Select or Premium plan starting at just $2.99.
articles.body: Thanks to Black Friday, you have two options to save on your Peacock subscription. You can now sign up for the ad-supported Select plan, usually $8.99 per month or $89.99 per year, for $2.99 for the first three months or $29.99 for the first year. The ad-supported Premium plan — which includes live sports, movies, and Peacock originals — is also only $8.99 per month for the first three months, or $89.99 ($40 off) for a year. Both offers are available to new and returning members through November 30th, but note that they will automatically renew at the then-current price if you don’t cancel before the renewal date. [Product: Peacock | While both plans are ad-supported, they differ quite a bit in what they offer. The Select plan lets you stream only TV shows that aired on NBC network channels, including NBC, Bravo, and Telemundo. If you just want to rewatch The Office and Law and Order, or catch new episodes of Below Deck, this plan is for you. The more expensive Premium plan, meanwhile, adds movies from studios like Universal Pictures and Dreamworks, along with live sports and Peacock Originals, like the Love Island spinoffs, Twisted Metal, and The Paper.

articles.title: Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
articles.summary: Nothing is launching the Ear Note on December 8th, a set of AI earbuds and charging case that can record and transcribe audio from calls or in-person conversations.
articles.body: Nothing’s new AI device is the Ear Note, a set of earbuds and their microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, with a connected app to manage the recordings, transcriptions and AI-generated summaries, similar to Apple’s new Watch feature and devices like Amazon’s Bee wearable. Nothing CEO Carl Pei demonstrated the new device to Bloomberg, but said the company hasn’t yet settled on a price ahead of a planned launch on December 8th. The report also says Nothing’s rumored plans for an AI smartwatch and smart glasses are delayed, while it will be “pursuing a more aggressive smartphone release schedule next year than it did in 2026.” In a post on X, Pei said this is “the first of many products building a hardware context layer for AI. Rather than ask you to carry a new product, we took something you already wear and trust and made it intelligent.” [Media: According to Bloomberg, the earbuds will “support interactions with various AI agents, including a more basic voice-control system developed by Nothing, letting users engage in back-and-forth conversations.” Users will also be able to record themselves with a “Talk” button on the case, like Nothing previously included on the Ear 3, which also has recording capabilities. Earlier this year, Nothing introduced an Audio Snapshot recording feature in the Ear 3A. Anker’s Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Max can also record directly to the earbuds’ case and generate AI transcripts and summaries in an app.

articles.title: HBO Max is offering one of the best Black Friday deals we’ve seen this year
articles.summary: HBO Max is offering 50 percent off for Black Friday. Here’s what to know about the discount, subscription plans, and what to watch.
articles.body: If you’ve been meaning to catch up on Lanterns or the latest season of The Gilded Age, Thanksgiving weekend is the perfect time to do so. And thanks to HBO Max’s new Black Friday deal, new and returning subscribers can now watch both shows for less. The streaming service is currently offering a 50 percent discount for Black Friday, bringing the price of its Basic With Ads plan down to $5.49 per month (about $6 off) for one year. The promotion runs through November 30th, and you can subscribe either via HBO Max or Amazon. [Product: HBO Max | HBO Max has plenty of great movies and shows to keep you entertained well into the new year, no matter which plan you choose. You’ll find a wide selection of TV shows, including Heated Rivalry, Dune: Prophecy, The White Lotus, Euphoria, and Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, alongside longtime favorites like Game of Thrones and The Big Bang Theory. There’s more on the way, too, including HBO’s highly anticipated Harry Potter series, which premieres on Christmas. There’s plenty to watch beyond TV, too. HBO Max’s extensive movie catalog currently includes films like Sinners, One Battle After Another, Marty Supreme, Backrooms, and Wuthering Heights. And if you’re a sports fan, both the Standard and Premium plans also include access to select live events from MLB, U.S. Soccer, the NCAA, and more. What you get ultimately depends on the subscription tier you choose. HBO Max’s Basic with Ads plan lets you stream on two devices at once but doesn’t include live sports. The ad-free Standard plan ($18.49 a month), meanwhile, adds live sports and up to 30 offline downloads. The Premium plan ($22.99 a month) adds a few more perks, including 4K streaming and Dolby Atmos with select titles, up to 100 downloads, and the ability to stream movies and shows on four devices simultaneously. That said, HBO currently isn’t offering discounts on either the Standard or Premium plans… at least not yet.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says he’ll be a ‘better CEO’ as staff applauds his return
articles.summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO today, and he told applauding employees that he’ll “be a better CEO the second time around,” as shown in a video.
articles.body: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s office as CEO today to a crowd of applauding employees who stood and filmed the cofounder’s first moments back. “Thank you all for the second chances. I’m gonna be a better CEO the second time around,” Huang said, as shown in a video of his return. [Media: [Media: Huang resigned as CEO on November 12th following reports of affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy as well as a direct report at Nvidia. Huang admitted two days before that he was “unfaithful to my wife.” President Trump, who had advocated for Huang to be reinstated ahead of it actually happening, was “totally involved” in his return, the White House said. In its press release about Huang’s reinstatement, the board of directors said it “received input from senior levels of the United States government” that made it “confident” that Huang’s reinstatement “poses no national security risk.” Trump asked Vice President JD Vance to help with the reinstatement over the weekend, including assisting the board to get “the assurances it needed,” The New York Times reported. “This is my first day at work,” Huang told staff today, according to a video reported on by Business Insider. “I’m terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this.”

articles.title: Asus co-CEO says its budget PCs “may move to 8GB” of memory due to RAM price hikes.
articles.summary:
Asus’s S.Y. Hsu said during the company’s earnings call that it can no longer pass “100 percent” of price increases onto consumers. Instead, Asus might “adjust the memory configuration” in budget and mid-range PCs from 16GB down to 8GB, citing Microsoft’s improvements to Windows 11 on devices with less RAM:
> It used to be that a mid to low tier machine will still ship with 16GB of memory, but now they may move to 8GB due to the memory cost increases. We have worked with Microsoft on this one. The old 16GB spec was really about ensuring user experience. On the new operating system, Microsoft has made adjustments such that even 8GB is able to yield an acceptable experience.
